memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD said to Moses, "Make a snake and put it up on a pole; anyone who is bitten can look at it and live." So Moses made a bronze snake and put it up on a pole. Then when anyone was bitten by a snake and looked at the bronze snake, they lived. - Num 21:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's remedy is startling in its simplicity. He does not remove the snakes at once. Instead He tells Moses to lift up a bronze snake on a pole. Anyone who was bitten had only to look at it, and they would live.

There was no medicine to take, no ritual to perform, no payment to make. Just a look of faith. The dying were asked simply to trust God's provision and turn their eyes toward it. Some may have thought it too easy to be true, yet those who looked, lived.

This is one of the clearest pictures of the gospel in all the Old Testament, and we do not have to guess at its meaning. Jesus Himself pointed to it. He said that just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life (John 3:14-15).

Sin has bitten us all, and its poison is death. But Christ was lifted up on the cross, and all who look to Him in faith are saved. Not by works, not by striving, but by looking to the Saviour. Have you looked to Him? Look, and live.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you trusting in your own efforts, or simply looking to Christ?
2. Does the simplicity of grace ever feel too easy to believe?
3. Who around you needs to hear this good news of "look and live"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Jesus, You were lifted up so that I could live. I look to You alone for salvation, trusting Your finished work on the cross. Amen.
